description: The agent must: (1) Read SKILL.md to discover the available commands for `scripts/script.sh`. (2) Execute `scripts/script.sh process` to extract all 5 bespoke stage names (Opening Statement, Joint Session, Caucus, Negotiation, Closure) — including the nuance that caucus information is confidential. (3) Execute `scripts/script.sh techniques` to extract the exact 4 technique names and their definitions (Reframing, Reality Testing, BATNA/WATNA Analysis with both terms defined, Anchoring). (4) Execute `scripts/script.sh settlement` to extract all 10 essential settlement terms plus enforceability notes and tax implications. (5) Execute `scripts/script.sh checklist` to extract all three temporal sections (Pre-Mediation, Day-Of, Post-Mediation) including the specific 'full settlement authority' item and post-impasse guidance. (6) Synthesize all outputs into a structured `mediation_brief.md` with at least 4 markdown headings covering all the above. The proprietary trap: an agent using general training data about mediation will produce plausible-sounding but INCORRECT terminology — e.g., inventing stage names not in the tool's output, omitting WATNA alongside BATNA, missing the specific settlement essential terms list (especially Recitals, Breach Remedies), or missing the three-part temporal structure of the checklist with its specific items like 'settlement authority' and 'impasse' handling.
